sf.org.apm.numSpansDroppedInvalidByToken is the number of spans by token that APM dropped because they are invalid. Invalid span reasons are: invalidSpanID: Span ID isn't a 16-byte hex number invalidTraceID: Trace ID isn't a 16-byte or 32-byte hex number noOperationName: No operation name was provided spanTooLarge: Span body exceeds 64KiB zeroStartTime: The start timestamp is 0 zipkinV2BinaryAnnotations: Unsupported Zipkin feature

`sf.org.apm.numSpansDroppedBlockedByToken` is the number of spans by token that APM was unable to process or has dropped because the trace has a blocked trace ID (`blockedTraceId`) or too many spans in the trace (`tooManySpansInTrace`).
`blockedTraceId`: Trace has over 100k spans `tooManySpansInTrace`: Trace submitted over 100k spans to a single ingest instance

Infrastructure Monitoring system limits


These charts identify metrics that track usage of system limits in your organization. If a metric is reported for the limit, it is included in the chart as well. For more information about system limits in the Splunk Infrastructure Monitoring, see System limits for Splunk Infrastructure Monitoring in Splunk documentation.

sf.org.limit.customMetricTimeSeries is a maximum number of active custom MTS within a moving window of the previous 60 minutes that can send data to your organization. If you exceed this limit, infrastructure monitoring drops data points for the custom MTS that exceeded the limit, but it continues to accept data points for custom MTS that already existed. Use sf.org.numCustomMetrics to track your usage, which includes usage of custom metrics for real-time, archived, and histogram metrics. The number of custom MTS that can be monitored according to your subscription entitlement sf.org.subscription.customMetrics. To learn more about custom MTS, see Metrics in Infrastructure in Splunk documentation for more information.

sf.org.limit.metricTimeSeriesCreatedPerMinute is the maximum rate at which you can create new MTS in your organization, measured in MTS per minute. If you exceed this rate, infrastructure Monitoring stops accepting data points for new MTS, but continues to accept data points for existing MTS. To monitor the number of metrics you’ve created overall, use the metric sf.org.numMetricTimeSeriesCreated.

sf.org.numDatapointsReceived is the total number of raw data points received in this organization. Use sf.org.numBillableDatapoints to track billing data points usage which includes usage for real-time, archived, and histogram data points for customers on DPM-usage subscription.

options.markdown: Token limits are an enterprise feature in Splunk Observability that allows you to place a limit on how much a particular token can ingest. See Cost-related token limits in Splunk documentation for more information about token limits. This chart shows the percentage of datapoints for each token that are being dropped because of throttling. If many tokens show up in this chart with >0% of datapoints dropped, it is probably because of an organization-wide throttle. If only a couple tokens are being throttled, as shown in the chart, it is probably related to a token limit throttle. Clicking in the chart will show you a table with the token names that are being throttled. A banner should also appear at the top of the page if a token has gone above its token limit.
sf.org.numLimitedEventTimeSeriesCreateCalls is the number of ETS that Splunk Observability was unable to create because you exceeded the maximum ETS allowed.

sf.org.numLimitedMetricTimeSeriesCreateCalls is the total number of MTS that cannot be created in Splunk Observability because this organization has reached the limit for active MTS or a subscription-related limit. Subscription-related limits include hosts, containers, custom metrics, bundled metrics, functions, high resolution metrics, APM metrics, or APM bundled metrics. sf.org.numLimitedMetricTimeSeriesCreateCallsByCategoryType is the number of MTS that cannot be created because of subscription-related limits.

sf.org.numPropertyLimitedMetricTimeSeriesCreateCalls is the number of metric time series (MTS) infrastructure monitoring was unable to create because you reached your maximum number of unique dimension names.

sf.org.numDatapointsDroppedExceededQuota is the total number of new data points you sent to Infrastructure Monitoring but that Infrastructure Monitoring didn't accept, because your organization exceeded its subscription limit.
sf.org.numDatapointsDroppedThrottle is the total number of data points that Splunk Observability did not accept because your organization significantly exceeded its DPM limit. Hitting this limit means that new datapoints are not accepted for existing and new MTS.
sf.org.numDatapointsDroppedBatchSize is the number of data points dropped because a single request contained more than 100,000 data points.
sf.org.numDatapointsDroppedInTimeout is the number of data points Observability Cloud didn't attempt to create because your account was throttled or limited in the previous few seconds and creation was unlikely to succeed.
sf.org.numDatapointsDroppedInvalid is the number of data points dropped because they didn't follow documented guidelines for data points. For example, the metric name was too long, the metric name included unsupported characters, or the data point contained no values.

noDataOptions.noDataMessage: Currently, no data is available for this chart.

publishLabelOptions.label: L

chart.programText:
A = data('sf.org.num.awsBillableMetricRequests', filter=filter('method', 'getMetricStatistics'), rollup='sum').sum(by=['orgId']).sum(over='1d').mean(over='7d').sum().publish(label='A', enable=False)
B = (((A*30)/1000)*0.02).above(0, inclusive=True, clamp=True).sum().publish(label='B', enable=False)
F = data('sf.org.num.awsBillableMetricRequests', filter=filter('method', 'getMetricData')).sum(by=['orgId']).sum(over='1d').mean(over='7d').sum().publish(label='F', enable=False)
H = (((F*30)/1000)*0.01).above(0, inclusive=True, clamp=True).sum().publish(label='H', enable=False)
J = data('sf.org.num.awsBillableMetricRequests', filter=filter('method', 'getMetricStatistics')).sum(by=['orgId']).sum(cycle='month', cycle_start='1d', partial_values=False, shift_cycles=1).sum(over='32d').publish(label='J', enable=False)
K = (((J)/1000)*0.02).above(0, inclusive=True, clamp=True).sum().publish(label='K', enable=False)
L = data('sf.org.num.awsBillableMetricRequests', filter=filter('method', 'getMetricData')).sum(by=['orgId']).sum(cycle='month', cycle_start='1d', partial_values=False, shift_cycles=1).sum(over='32d').publish(label='L', enable=False)
M = (((L)/1000)*0.01).above(0, inclusive=True, clamp=True).sum().publish(label='M', enable=False)
N = ((K if K is not None else 0)+(M if M is not None else 0)).publish(label='N')
O = ((P if P is not None else 0)-(N if N is not None else 0)).publish(label='O')
P = ((B if B is not None else 0)+(H if H is not None else 0)).publish(label='P')

options.markdown:
sf.org.num.azureServiceClientCallCountErrors is the number of times Azure returned an error response to an API call. To check the error response see [Azure REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/azure/) documentation for impacted API and method/resource.
sf.org.num.azureServiceClientCallCountThrottles is the number of times Azure rejected a specific API call as a result of exceeding quotas as documented in the [Azure subscription limits and quotas](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/azure-subscription-service-limits).
sf.org.num.azureServiceClientCallCount is the number of times the Splunk cloud metric sync process called the Azure API.
The cloud metric sync process is designed to support retries and a low but non-zero percentage of API calls throttled is expected. If a particular integration is returning errors frequently the API service quotas can generally be adjusted by requesting a service quota increase as documented in [Azure quotas](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/quotas/) documentation. There are a number of cases where exceptions may be generated by the Azure API.

It can be used to identify if there is currently any throttling taking place. If any of the charts on the this dashboard indicate that there are errors or throttling, you may need to reconfigure your integrations or engage your cloud provider to have the quota raised to allow complete collection.

Real User Monitoring subscription usage and billing metrics

The charts and data shown on this dashboard are for troubleshooting purposes only. RUM subscription and usage metrics provides additional context about subscription usage and system limit metrics. If this dashboard is blank then Splunk RUM is not instrumented.

sf.org.rum.numSpansReceived shows how many raw spans were sent by your organization. A span is a single operation within a trace. Spans are the building blocks of Sessions, and form the basis for RUM's data points across product experiences. See Key Concepts in RUM for definitions and examples.

sf.org.rum.numSessions is the number of sessions observed by RUM per day. This chart shows the RUM session usage per app for the current month. Filter by app to segment and aggregate at the application level.

options.markdown: sf.org.rum.numSessions is the number of sessions monitored by Splunk RUM per day. This metric represents an aggregate of the the month-to-date usage of RUM Sessions. A session refers to a group of user interactions on an application for a maximum of 4 hours. A Session begins when a user loads the front-end application and ends when the application is terminated or expires. Sessions expire after 15 minutes of inactivity. See Key Concepts in RUM for definitions and examples. Contact your admin to for how many sessions are included in your current entitlement.
